observations.text: SP executed the Go Around at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing the sequence of power application, pitch attitude and clean-up of the A/C configuration. The decision to go around was taken only after the IP's command and the flap and gear retraction was called item by item; the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP was regained with the IP flying part of the climb-out, altitude excursions reaching 350 feet. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recognition that landing is not ensured and unassisted initiation of the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual are expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP executed the Go Around using only the IP's verbal indications, without any IP control input on the stick or the throttle. Power was advanced and the A/C configuration cleaned according to standard procedures after prompting, within the airspeed limitations for flap and gear retraction, and the onset of stall characteristics was not allowed at any point. Airspeed deviations were contained at 20 knots and altitude at 300 feet against the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, recognized and corrected with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP responded to the IP's Go Around command without delay and flew the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual without IP's intervention. Minor errors in the sequence of the clean-up produced an airspeed deviation of 15 knots and a climb 200 feet above the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, both recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. The exit heading was regained within 8 degrees of the runway heading and no stall characteristics were allowed to develop. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP made the right decision to Go Around in a timely manner when landing was no longer ensured, and executed the maneuver with accuracy and speed. Power, pitch attitude and clean-up of the A/C configuration were applied in the order prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual, each retraction within its airspeed limitation. The landing pattern altitude reported in LAP was held within 100 feet, the airspeed within 7 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees, with no IP intervention required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP recognized that landing was not ensured at the earliest available point and executed the Go Around immediately, on his own initiative in the first pattern and on the Contact Car Officer's command in the second. The standard procedure was flown with exceptional precision, deviations remaining negligible at 50 feet from the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, 3 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees in exit heading. Configuration clean-up was completed well within the airspeed limitations, the wings were kept level throughout and no approach to stall characteristics occurred. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power application technique that advanced the PCL only partially before rotating to the go-around pitch attitude, did not follow the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not clean the A/C configuration within the airspeed limitations. Airspeed decayed 25 knots below the briefed go-around value and the A/C sank 400 feet below the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the climb. Repetition of the power, pitch and configuration sequence on the ground trainer is required.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognised unsafe condition, did not make the right decision to Go Around in a timely manner when the landing was no longer ensured. The approach was continued past the point at which a correction was still available and the recovery was started only when the IP directed it, the A/C descending 450 feet below the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP before power was applied. The IP executed part of the climb-out and the clean-up of the A/C configuration. Stating the go-around decision aloud at the moment it is recognized is required.

SP completed the Go Around within the standard expected for this training unit, executing power application, pitch attitude and configuration clean-up after the IP's verbal indications and without any IP control input. Deviations reached the limit of the desired standard, with 300 feet against the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP and 20 knots in airspeed, recognized and corrected with delay in both patterns. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the deviation and a shorter interval between the go-around order and the first control input are expected to improve in the following sorties.

SP responded immediately to the go-around order given by ATC and flew the maneuver without IP's intervention. Minor errors in the timing of the flap retraction produced an airspeed deviation of 15 knots and a 200 feet excursion above the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, each recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. No onset of stall characteristics was allowed and the runway heading was regained within 8 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP decided to Go Around on his own initiative as soon as the landing was no longer ensured, and executed the maneuver with accuracy and speed. The A/C configuration was cleaned according to standard procedures and within the airspeed limitations, in the order prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Altitude was contained within 120 feet of the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees, with no verbal indication required from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Go Around immediately on the Contact Car Officer's command and, in the second pattern, on his own initiative before the IP had assessed the approach. Deviations were negligible throughout, with 50 feet against the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, 3 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees in exit heading. Power application and configuration clean-up were exact and comfortably inside the airspeed limitations, the pattern was re-entered in sequence and no stall characteristics developed at any stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a pitch technique that rotated the A/C well beyond the go-around attitude before the power reached the required setting, did not prevent the onset of stall characteristics during the transition to the climb. The stall warning activated and the airspeed fell 30 knots below the briefed go-around value, with the result that the IP took the controls, unloaded the A/C and completed the clean-up of the configuration. Practice of the power-first, pitch-second sequence of the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required before the next pattern sortie.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorised recovery sequence, did not execute the Go Around without any delay when the order was given by the Contact Car Officer on short final. The first control input came several seconds after the order and consisted of flap retraction before power application, with the result that the A/C descended 400 feet below the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP and the IP directed and executed part of the recovery. The go-around sequence must be reviewed to the point of immediate recall.

SP, due to a scan that remained on the runway during the transition to the climb, did not follow the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual in the order prescribed and delayed the gear retraction until prompted. The airspeed deviated 20 knots from the briefed go-around value and the climb reached 300 feet above the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and with delay. No IP control input was required. A deliberate transition to the flight instruments once the climb is established is required.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not maintain the pattern parameters while cleaning the A/C configuration during the Go Around. The airspeed increased 20 knots beyond the briefed value and the exit heading diverged 10 degrees from the runway heading, both recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and without IP control input. Re-establishing the cross check of the control and performance instruments immediately after each retraction is required.

SP executed the Go Around within the desired standards for this training unit, responding without delay to the IP's order and cleaning the A/C configuration within the airspeed limitations. Minor errors in the initial power setting twice produced airspeed deviations of 15 knots and a 200 feet excursion above the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more precise initial power setting and a steadier climb attitude are expected to reduce these deviations in the following sorties.

SP made the right decision to Go Around in a timely manner when the landing was not ensured and executed the maneuver with accuracy and speed, without IP's intervention. The standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual was followed in sequence and the configuration was cleaned within the airspeed limitations. The landing pattern altitude reported in LAP was respected with deviations within 100 feet, the airspeed was held within 7 knots and the exit heading within 4 degrees, with no onset of stall characteristics. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Go Around both on his own initiative and on ATC order, with an immediate and exact response in each case. Deviations were negligible, with the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP held within 50 feet, the airspeed within 3 knots and the exit heading within 2 degrees. Configuration clean-up, trim and re-entry into the pattern were handled with ease by night as well as by day, and the wings were kept level with no approach to stall characteristics at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a technique that retracted the flaps in a single selection immediately after power application, did not clean the A/C configuration according to standard procedures and within the airspeed limitations. The A/C sank 400 feet below the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP with the stall warning active, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the climb. Review of the flap retraction schedule and of its airspeed gates is required before the next pattern sortie.

SP, due to continuation of the plan after the information that invalidated it had already been received, did not make the right decision to Go Around in a timely manner when the preceding A/C had not cleared the runway. The approach was flown to the point at which the IP had to order and then execute the Go Around, the A/C passing 350 feet below the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP before power was applied. Treating the published go-around criteria as decision points rather than as advisory information is required.

SP, due to an unrehearsed sequence in which the gear was selected up before a positive rate of climb was confirmed, did not follow the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual during the Go Around. The airspeed reached 20 knots from the briefed go-around value and the climb 300 feet above the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and with delay, without IP control input. Chair-flying of the full go-around sequence before the next sortie is required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not respond immediately to the go-around order given by ATC and attempted to complete the landing checks before applying power. Execution was achieved only after repeated verbal indications from the IP, the exit heading diverging 10 degrees from the runway heading and the altitude 300 feet from the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, recognized and corrected with delay. No IP control input was required. Shedding the secondary task at the moment the go-around order is received is required.

SP, due to a rudder input that lagged the power application, did not hold the runway heading during the initial climb of the Go Around. The exit heading diverged 8 degrees and the airspeed 15 knots from the briefed go-around value, both recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. The configuration was cleaned within the airspeed limitations and no stall characteristics were allowed to develop.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not execute the Go Around without any delay once the order was given by the Contact Car Officer. The delayed first power input produced a 200 feet excursion below the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP and a 15 knots airspeed deviation, both recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The standard procedure was thereafter completed in the prescribed order and within the airspeed limitations.

SP executed the Go Around at the desired standard for this training unit, deciding on his own initiative when the landing was not ensured and following the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual with accuracy and speed. Deviations remained inside the desired code but sat at its upper end on both patterns, with 140 feet against the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, 10 knots in airspeed and 5 degrees in exit heading. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a steadier initial pitch attitude is expected to move these deviations towards the middle of the desired band in the following sorties.

SP recognized on each occasion that the landing was not ensured before the IP had assessed it, and executed the Go Around immediately and without hesitation, by day and by night. The standard procedure was flown with exceptional precision, deviations remaining negligible at 40 feet from the landing pattern altitude reported in LAP, 3 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees in exit heading. Configuration clean-up was completed well inside the airspeed limitations, the pattern was re-entered in the correct sequence and the required radio calls were made without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.
